decision: The pinned author-linked MIT dataset card clears the repository's data-license policy for a task-scoped cross-sensory object-retrieval fit. An object-disjoint 400/100/100 split is frozen by seed 17. A deterministic 20-point train/validation sample is complete and hash-verified; masked RGB crops retain some printed object/package text and some detached mask fragments. Treat this as a data-control requirement, not a reason to infer benchmark leakage. Keep evaluation media unopened. Before fitting, freeze the task/gallery protocol and text/background controls. Do not claim semantic object/material reasoning or broad Omni quality.
limitations: The official project page links to the Hub card but does not repeat the license in its own text; the license grant is recorded from the pinned author-linked card.

The archive index has no root-level machine-readable description or split table; the paper's object descriptions are not needed for identity retrieval but are required for semantic object/material decisions.
The reported paper baseline uses a different protocol and is not this project's result.
The 20-point visual screen is a small manual sample and does not estimate corpus-wide text or mask-artifact prevalence.
Some target objects are composite or labeled packages; printed text is present on the target itself, so image crops do not remove all lexical cues.
Current free disk space is below the full archive size and far below the official uncompressed size.
